ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and foreign counsel against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, Egypt's national Terrorist Persons and Entities List maintained by the EMLCU and the National Committee for Combating Terrorism, the FATF Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring list, and World Bank sanctions lists. Enhanced due diligence is compulsory for politically exposed persons, requiring source-of-wealth documentation, senior-management approval, and continuous monitoring under FATF Recommendation 12 and Egyptian Law No. 80 of 2002.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) Unified Electronic Company Registration Portal — www.gafi.gov.eg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be in Arabic; a Latin-script transliteration may also be registered. The Arabic name must be unique, not contrary to public order or morals, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. The legal-form suffix 'LLC' or Arabic equivalent must be included and fully transliterated. No name implying prohibited activities, public institutions, or religious connotations will be accepted without special authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written refusal from GAFI, the applicant may submit a reconsideration request to the GAFI Deputy Chairman for Company Affairs within 10 working days, attaching the refusal memo and a revised name or a legal memorandum addressing specificity. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the Egyptian State Council (Administrative Courts) within 60 days. An interim application may be made for expedited clearance of an alternative name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not accepted for a licensed commercial litigation and arbitration firm. The Egyptian Ministry of Justice requires a physical, staffed office with professional signage, secure records storage, and defined client-reception facilities. Executive suite arrangements may only be acceptable if the suite is a dedicated physical office and the legal entity maintains a full-time presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 70% likelihood of a pre-licensing physical inspection and a continuing risk of unannounced spot inspections after licensing; the risk is regarded as high due to the regulated professional-services nature of the activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Companies Law, as amended) Arts. 12–23 (Limited Liability Company); Executive Regulations issued by Ministerial Decree No. 887 of 1981; Law No. 72 of 2017 (Investment Law) Art. 42 (deemed silence approval); Law No. 4 of 2018 (One-Stop-Shop facilitation amendments); Law No. 68 of 1947 (Notaries Law) for memorandum notarization; Law No. 17 of 1983 (Advocacy Law) Arts. 20–30 and 62–63, as amended by Law No. 1 of 2015, for law-office licensing and foreign counsel admission.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Investor Services Center, in coordination with the Commercial Registry Directorate of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association (Aqd El Ta'sis) and the GAFI electronic Company Registration Form (Core Form S-2), filed jointly with a Commercial Registry application for the issuance of the Incorporation Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum stated capital for a multi-member LLC under Law 159/1981 as amended; stated capital must nevertheless be fully subscribed and lawful currency of Egypt. One-person LLCs must evidence full payment of stated capital via a notarized declaration; where stated capital exceeds EGP 250,000, a bank receipt or escrow attestation from a Central Bank of Egypt licensed bank must be submitted to GAFI.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That each incorporator subscribes to the number of shares set against his name in the unanimous subscription schedule, and that the approximately stated share capital of EGP 250,000 be and is hereby declared satisfied in cash in full; (2) That the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [address] in Cairo, Egypt, with competence before the competent courts; (3) That [Name] be and is hereby appointed General Manager, with sole signature authority for banking, registry, and judicial acts; (4) That [Name] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary and AML Compliance Officer, with responsibility for the IOLTA trust account and for all filings with GAFI and the Egyptian Tax Authority; and (5) That all officers shall hold office until lawfully revoked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Commercial Registry Pre-Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center and the Commercial Registry Directorate (Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade), via the GAFI electronic portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online name reservation application with three alternative names in Arabic. The registrar screens against the national Commercial Registry index and GAFI's blacklist under Law 159/1981 Art. 13. The approved name, followed by the suffix 'LLC', is reserved for 60 days pending filing.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (GAFI Form R-1)
Certified copies of passports of all incorporators
Power of Attorney, if an agent submits filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity, an administrative grievance may be lodged with the Commercial Registry Director within 15 days; alternatively, the second or third alternative name is activated immediately without an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Approval, and Notarization of the Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary Office (Ministry of Justice Notary Authority) and GAFI-approved service offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a bilingual memorandum, with the Arabic text controlling, containing incorporators' full identity details, share capital, in-kind or cash contributions, management rights, and the legal representation clause. Insert a scope clause strictly limited to cross-border commercial litigation, arbitration, and asset tracing, consistent with the Advocacy Law and Bar Association practice rules. All incorporators or their authorized attorneys must sign before a notary; Arabic translations of foreign documents must be certified.
required_dossiers: Draft memorandum of association in Arabic
Certified passport copies of all incorporators
Original Power of Attorney, duly legalized, where signatures are delegated
Notarized certificate of lawful residence and legal capacity (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises signature or capacity queries, submit corrected signature attestations or an apostilled/consular-legalized power of attorney and re-tender the memorandum to the same notary office; no additional statutory fee is due for correction of ministerial omissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop Filing and Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center (One-Stop-Shop), Commercial Registry Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically submit the Core Form S-2 together with the notarized memorandum, pay all official fees through the GAFI treasury or bank portal, and file the lease contract of the registered office location. GAFI verifies the file, obtains mutual clearance with the Commercial Registry and Tax Authority, and issues the Incorporation Certificate (commercial registration number) within the statutory timeframe.
required_dossiers: Notarized memorandum of association and notary receipt
Name reservation certificate
Registered office lease contract duly stamped
GAFI Core Form S-2 and fee payment receipt
IDs and criminal record certificates of managers
Bank attestation of fully paid capital (where capital exceeds EGP 250,000)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deficiency memo, correct the stated items within 30 days; failure to respond triggers rejection, in which case a complete refiling and a grievance to the GAFI Chairman will cure in 15 days under the Investment Law Art. 42 deemed-approval procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Tax Card, and VAT Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Tax Card and E-Invoicing Departments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC under Law No. 91 of 2005 at the competent ETA branch, applying for the unified Tax Card and Value Added Tax certificate under Law No. 67 of 2016. Enroll the entity in the ETA E-Invoicing and E-Receipt system after obtaining a commercial registration number. Use the legal-services activity code (ISIC 6910) and preserve cash-basis privilege for litigation proceeds.
required_dossiers: Incorporation certificate and commercial registration card
Tax card application (Form 21)
Notarized memorandum and lease contract
Directors' IDs and passport-style photos
Bank account opening confirmation from a licensed Egyptian bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance exceeds the 20-day statutory limit, file an ombudsman complaint at the ETA headquarters; provisional tax clearance can be requested for banking and licensing purposes, and the e-invoicing enrollment may be activated in parallel after the first tax submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the IOLTA Trust Account and AML Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Bank of Egypt licensed banks (e.g., National Bank of Egypt or Banque Misr) and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open two bank accounts on behalf of the LLC: a general operations account and a segregated IOLTA/trust account for client funds under Banking Law No. 194 of 2020. Submit the beneficial ownership register to the bank and execute the EMLCU Customer Due Diligence form, appointing the AML Compliance Officer identified in the Board Resolution. Ensure the trust account ledger strictly records client disbursements and retains 5 years of records.
required_dossiers: Incorporation certificate and tax card
Directors' and ultimate beneficial owners' KYC documents
AML compliance policy and beneficial ownership register
Board resolution designating signatories and the trust account purpose
IOLTA account opening application and undertaking to comply with Law No. 80 of 2002
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, supply updated source-of-funds evidence and apostilled beneficial ownership certificates; if the request is denied, apply to another CBE-authorized bank, or file a complaint with CBE's Consumer Protection Unit for an expedited review within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bar Association Registration and Legal Practice License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Bar Association (Nakabet El Mohameen), Ministry of Justice Foreign Lawyers Admission Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the firm at the Bar Association's Lawyers' Registry (Qalam El Qaid) as a professional law office (Maktab Mohamaat) using the Egyptian partners' valid Bar membership. For foreign partners, file a separate application to the Ministry of Justice for the registration of foreign legal consultants limited to international arbitration and advisory assignments, without rights of audience before Egyptian courts unless an Egyptian-licensed counsel appears. Present the Commercial Registry certificate and pay the annual practice fee.
required_dossiers: Bar membership certificates of Egyptian partners
Certified copy of the commercial registration certificate
LLC memorandum and Bar-drafted firm charter statement
No-criminal-record certificate for each partner
Lease or ownership deed of the office premises
Samples of engagement letters and the IOLTA trust account confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Bar rejects the firm application, appeal to the Bar Disciplinary Committee within 15 days. If the Ministry of Justice delays foreign counsel registration, the firm may provisionally operate for arbitration mandates only; final licensure follows within 30 days of a written reminder and may be contested via the Administrative Courts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Egyptian Bar Association — Practice Licensing Board, in coordination with the Ministry of Justice (Foreign Lawyers Admission Commission) and the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Legal Practice License (Tarkhees Maktab Mohamaat) — Professional Practice Certificate under Law No. 17 of 1983, as amended, including a limited Foreign Legal Consultancy Permit for cross-border arbitration and advisory work

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — Ministry of Environment, applying Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A (White List) — Environmental registration only; no full EIA Report is mandated for professional office use within an urban commercial building. If the firm later installs document-shredding or archival storage for third-party records exceeding 500 m², a Category B environmental screening (Form 63, low-impact services) will be required before operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to municipal sewers must comply with Law No. 48 of 1982 and Ministerial Decree No. 92 of 2013: BOD ≤ 60 mg/L, COD ≤ 80 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L; no volatile organic compound (VOC) or fossil-fuel combustion emission sources are permitted for court-adjacent chambers; secured paper waste must be transferred only to EEAA-licensed recycling contractors, with manifest records retained for 5 years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (Shahadat Itfa') from the General Administration of Civil Defense, inspected for exit capacity, smoke detectors, 4ABC dry-chemical extinguishers at a ratio of one per 75 m², and an approved evacuation plan; structural load safety clearance of the rented chambers by an Engineering Syndicate licensed statutory engineer; workplace compliance and occupational clearance under Law No. 12 of 2003 (Labor Law) and Ministerial Decree No. 133 of 2003, covering ventilation, illuminated signage, an accessible client meeting room, and a fire-rated (60-minute) secure document vault for litigation archives and client funds records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Ministry of Finance; official taxpayer portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing and digital-stamping platform: https://einvoice.eta.gov.eg; TIN validation gateway: https://id.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate at the GAFI one-stop shop and obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate (CR). Step 2 — File the ETA general tax registration (Form 1 for corporate taxpayers) within 30 days of the CR date, submitting the Articles of Association, head-office title or lease, board-resolution extract appointing the tax representative, and identity documents of shareholders and directors; the ETA issues the unified Tax Card bearing the statutory 9-digit TIN. Step 3 — Register for VAT under Law No. 67/2016 once taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed the EGP 500,000 mandatory threshold; the ETA then issues a separate VAT ID linked to the TIN. Step 4 — Complete e-invoicing activation by uploading the entity's digital signature certificate, validating the ERP system against the ETA's API test environment, and receiving the e-invoice clearance UUID code. Step 5 — File monthly VAT returns by the 20th of the month following each tax period, quoting the TIN and VAT ID in all filings; foreign-owned LLCs must simultaneously maintain the Central Bank-compliant FX repatriation file for non-resident fee receipts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egyptian law does not provide check-the-box, pass-through, or hybrid-mismatch elections; an EG LLC is per se opaque and taxed at entity level on worldwide income at the corporate income tax rate. Available elections are limited to: (1) GAFI Investment Law No. 72/2017 incentive election (flat-rate tax bands, customs and VAT reliefs for qualifying projects inside designated zones); (2) consolidated income tax filing election for Egyptian group companies under Article 57 of Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 (ministerial approval); (3) SME presumptive-profit election under the Unified Tax Law amendments (Law No. 1/2022) where turnover bands do not exceed EGP 20 million; and (4) e-invoice validation-mode election (real-time API vs. web-portal batch clearance). None of these alters the entity-level liability of the LLC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Egyptian Value Added Tax (VAT) — Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended by Law No. 3/2018 and Law No. 173/2022; Executive Regulations issued by Decree No. 66/2017
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies for mandatory VAT registration; EGP 50,000 for voluntary registration (small traders subject to simplified schedule); e-invoicing is compulsory for all VAT-registered persons irrespective of turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt operates a centralized fiscal clearance mandate, not merely an e-reporting obligation. Every B2B invoice (and, in phased sectors, B2C e-receipts) must be composed in the ETA's XML/JSON schema, digitally signed, transmitted in real time at the moment of issuance, and validated by the ETA's clearance engine. The engine verifies the VAT ID white-list, buyer identity, invoice legal rules, mandatory Arabic/English fields, and the applicable zero-rating code; upon acceptance the ETA returns the official invoice UUID and QR-style digital stamp, and only this ETA-stamped invoice is legally valid for VAT deduction and export zero-rating. Rejected invoices are deemed not issued from a fiscal-law perspective, exposing the taxpayer to Article 74–76 penalties. Machine-to-machine API, sFTP batch, and web-portal channels are permitted with OAuth2-enabled digital certificates; the export zero-rated invoice requires a separate ETA zero-rating code and reconciliation with the monthly return schedule.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to services that are genuinely exported, including cross-border commercial litigation, arbitration, and asset-tracing services, provided: (i) the service recipient is a non-resident person holding no Egyptian permanent establishment; (ii) the contractual seat of performance (arbitral or judicial forum) and the legal benefit of the service are located outside Egypt; (iii) the deliverables are transmitted offshore; and (iv) consideration is paid in foreign currency by external remittance into an Egyptian bank account. Services enjoyed or consummated inside Egypt (e.g., Egyptian court hearings, enforcement of Egyptian judgments, onshore discovery) do not qualify and are taxable at 14% unless exempt under a specific schedule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (AVR Form) — required only where goods accompany or proceed from the litigation (e.g., inspection samples); for pure services the zero-rated services declaration on the VAT return operates in its place

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill — evidencing physical export of any documentary or evidential exhibits; for digital legal services, the ETA e-invoice transmission record and off-platform delivery logs satisfy the export-evidence rule
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the Egyptian receiving bank, CRR-verified, proving receipt of foreign-currency consideration and matched by FX conversion records
Signed cross-border legal services agreement with non-resident client plus seat-of-dispute or arbitration clause outside Egypt
ETA e-invoice export clearance record bearing the zero-rating code and the official ETA UUID
Performance dossier: foreign arbitration or court docket numbers, foreign counsel retainers, and off-Egypt delivery reports
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and the Central Bank of Egypt jointly audit export-service proceeds and remittance evidence. If foreign-currency receipts are not repatriated to Egypt within the 180-day statutory deadline, the zero rating is retrospectively reversed, the supply must be re-characterized as a domestic taxable supply at 14%, and the ETA may reopen the preceding five fiscal years to claw back unpaid VAT with statutory late-payment interest and a fine of not less than the evaded tax. Deliberate or fraudulent zero-rating claims (false remittance certificates, fictitious offshore seats, nominee foreign entities) constitute tax evasion causing imprisonment and monetary fines under Articles 74–76 of Law No. 67/2016, cancellation of e-invoicing clearance privileges for up to two years, public registration on the ETA tax-evasion list, and suspension of GAFI investment incentives; the ETA also notifies the Egyptian AML unit and the competent professional licensing board (Ministry of Justice) for disciplinary debarment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) – البنك المركزي المصري, established under Law No. 163 of 2022 issuing the new Central Bank and Banking System Law (replacing Law No. 88 of 2003). The CBE holds exclusive jurisdiction over foreign-exchange licensing, banking supervision, capital-flow registration, and monetary policy. The CBE coordinates with the Egyptian Money Laundering Combating Unit (EMLCU), the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), and the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) for cross-border treasury, AML, and investment-entry controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations, guaranteeing current-account convertibility. Since the 6 March 2024 FX liberalization, the CBE unified the official and parallel exchange rates under a flexible EGP regime; current-account service receipts (legal fees, arbitration disbursements, settlement proceeds) are freely convertible and transferable through authorized banks without CBE pre-approval. Capital-account transactions (inbound equity injections, shareholder loans, share-transfer proceeds, liquidation distributions) remain subject to CBE documentation-based validation and bank-level balance-of-payments coding under BPM6. Profit and equity remittance hurdles: the remitting bank must verify the original inflow trail (GAFI investment certificate, CBE foreign-currency inflow registration), confirm the entity holds a valid commercial registration and tax card, and obtain an automatic tax-clearance acknowledgment from the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA). No centralized profit-repatriation moratorium exists post-2024; however, banks retain documentary discretion and enhanced due diligence for remittances exceeding EGP 1 million equivalent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion ratio applies to export or service receipts. Since the 2016 float, and confirmed by the March 2024 unified-rate reform, exporters and service providers (including cross-border law firms) may retain 100% of foreign-currency proceeds in FX accounts at authorized banks without surrender to the CBE. Statutory repatriation timeline: goods exports – proceeds must be credited to an Egyptian bank within six months from the bill-of-lading or airway-bill date, extendable to twelve months upon documented CBE-approved bank justification; services exports – proceeds must be received within ninety days from the invoice date unless a longer contractual credit period is evidenced and bank-approved. For EG_LLC, legal-service export receivables must flow through the Egyptian banking system within the ninety-day window; late repatriation triggers CBE administrative sanctions under the Central Bank Law and is treated by EMLCU as an AML red flag.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Revolut, Payoneer, MultiPass) to hold IOLTA-style client balances in Egypt. A non-resident EMI cannot accept deposits from an Egyptian-licensed LLC or provide segregated trust accounts without a CBE e-money institution license under the Central Bank Law; the CBE has not recognized any foreign EMI as an authorized custodian of client money. Offshore EMIs may operate only as ancillary inbound/outbound corridor rails (e.g., receiving a USD remittance and forwarding via SWIFT/MT103) provided funds do not remain parked on the EMI ledger. Domestic fintechs (Fawry, Paymob, MNT-Halan, Contact by EFG Hermes) are rated Medium for operational collections and invoice reconciliation but are legally barred from operating interest-bearing client trust accounts; they may serve as parallel collection rails under a merchant agreement with automatic daily sweep to a Tier-1 bank escrow account. Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) front-end onboarding is permitted only where the custody ledger resides with a CBE-licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of EG_LLC. Under CBE AML Rule No. 117 of 2022 and EMLCU instructions, the statutory manager, authorized signatories, and any UBO holding 25% or more must attend an in-person compliance interview at the account-opening branch. Remote video-KYC is accepted only for Egyptian-resident individuals holding a valid national ID; non-resident principals may instead delegate to a notarized Egyptian attorney-in-fact, but the attorney must appear physically and present the original certified power of attorney (wakala) legalized by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the competent Egyptian consulate. Minimum physical dossier at the interview: original commercial register extract (ش.ت.), valid tax card, GAFI incorporation certificate, board resolution fixing account signatories, audited or bank-reviewed financial statement, signed AML questionnaire, and the corporate seal (kheem) pressed on all account forms. Non-Egyptian legal entities in the ownership chain must provide certified passport copies, proof of foreign registration, and an English/Arabic certified translation of all corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO opacity – EG_LLC ownership traces to foreign shareholder firms and an arbitration-law manager without Egyptian tax residency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original GAFI Beneficial Ownership Register confirmation and incorporation file; certified true-copies of UBO passports with Egyptian consular legalization; 12-month bank reference letter from the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction; Egyptian Tax Authority tax-clearance certificate; sworn source-of-funds declaration tracing the original capital injection; board resolution approved by all shareholders with certified English-Arabic translation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client-money concentration – single escrow account receiving litigation funding and settlement proceeds from multiple foreign counterparties without an IOLTA statute in Egypt
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client retainer and engagement letters per underlying matter; escrow agreement executed between the bank, EG_LLC, and the payer-client under Civil Code escrow principles; per-matter ledger and monthly reconciliation policy; source-of-funds declarations from each foreign client; court or arbitration reference numbers (ICC, LCIA, CRCICA, DIAC case IDs); nil-sanction screen (UN, OFAC, EU) for every client and counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-risk ambiguity – Egyptian Bar Association (EBA) membership and the firm's revenue mix unverified in the bank's risk engine for legal-services accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EBA practicing license and membership certificate; commercial registry extract listing 'legal activities – ISIC 6910'; professional indemnity insurance policy; 12-month bank statements of the firm's existing operating account showing low-risk billing patterns; prior-period tax declarations; compliance officer appointment letter and organizational chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Judgment and award flows – foreign arbitral award or court judgment directs payment into EG_LLC's Egyptian account, triggering FATF red flags on legal structures and third-party fund origins
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized deed of assignment of proceeds; final award or court judgment authenticated by apostille or consular legalization; legal opinion mapping the award to EG_LLC's standing and entitlement; chain-of-title documents for the underlying receivable; bank payment instruction carrying a full purpose description in English and Arabic; EMLCU special-report template completed for any counterparty identified as a politically exposed person.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for foreign shareholder capital injection into EG_LLC: real-time SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for bank-to-bank repositioning) from the foreign shareholder's bank to the EG_LLC USD/EGP account at a CBE-licensed bank. The receiving bank must code the credit under BPM6 'Direct Investment – Equity Injection' (CBE account classification 'AE-1 Capital Contribution'); the remitting bank must quote the purpose code 'Capital Investment' under the CBE Balance-of-Payments Instruction and insert the GAFI investment file number in SWIFT field 70 (Remittance Information). Before the first credit, EG_LLC must file a Foreign Currency Inflow Declaration with the CBE through its account bank, attaching: GAFI license, commercial register extract, tax card, shareholders' resolution, and a notarized capital certificate. Enhanced due diligence applies where the injection exceeds USD 100,000 equivalent, requiring source-of-funds confirmations from the remitting bank, UBO passport copies, and proof of the foreign bank's regulatory licensing. Non-cash contributions (receivables or IP) require a CBE-approved valuation report by the General Authority for Investment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 with full correspondence for court filing fees, expert witness fees, overseas counsel, arbitrator fees, and settlement distributions; each MT103 must reference the invoice or award number and quote a CBE 'invisible current transaction' service-export code for automatic clearing. Commercial LC alternative: Egyptian banks issue sight or term documentary letters of credit only where the underlying is a goods trade or a law-firm milestone reimbursement tied to a sealed settlement agreement; a standby LC may be used for cross-border escrow margin obligations. Documentary gate and thresholds: post-2024 deregulation removes statutory per-transfer caps, but banks apply enhanced review at USD 50,000 equivalent and require for settlement payments above USD 100,000 a certified copy of the final award or settlement agreement approved by the competent court. Egyptian Tax Authority validation: outbound service remittances are gate-checked against the 15–20% withholding regime on foreign service fees unless a treaty relief certificate under a tax treaty (e.g., Egypt-UK, Egypt-France, Egypt-UAE DTAAs) is presented; the paying bank must obtain a stamped tax-clearance acknowledgment to release the wire.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards (USD/EGP, EUR/EGP) with tenors up to 12 months, permitted only where EG_LLC evidences an underlying retainer-receivable or payable-invoice exposure to the dealing bank (underlying-exposure test).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EGP for tenors up to 24 months, executed offshore or with CBE-approved onshore banks, cash-settled in USD with no EGP delivery; a documented hedging rationale is required for onshore booking.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, USD/EGP) under ISDA/CSA agreements where the firm carries multi-currency costs (EUR arbitration-seat expenses, USD court disbursements), subject to board-approved treasury policy and a bank credit-line approval.
FX options with capped-cost structures as a permissible overlay for settlement-contingency exposure, classified as non-speculative and evidenced in the firm's treasury policy.

Currency-swap-linked escrow structures permitting USD-denominated collateral substitution where client funds are held pending award enforcement, eligible at Tier-1 banks holding CBE derivative licenses and subject to full asset-liability documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of EGP 1,000–5,000 plus monthly late-payment interest of 2% on unpaid tax; persistent non-filing may trigger asset seizure, bank account freezing, and criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements Filing with GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Corporate Registry and Company Oversight Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the fiscal year end and before the Annual General Assembly meeting; for calendar-year entities by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the 6-month window triggers an administrative warning and a fine; repeated non-filing for two consecutive years may lead to judicial strike-off or commencement of liquidation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry Annual Renewal and Rate Fee Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the expiry date endorsed on the commercial registration record; in practice on or before 31 December of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs incremental late fees of EGP 100–500 per month and a temporary suspension marking on the registry record; continued non-renewal results in administrative strike-off and restriction of transactions with banks and notaries.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner and Shareholder Register Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI – Legal and Compliance Directorate, AML Unit Records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation filed by 31 March in respect of beneficial ownership details as of the previous year-end; within 30 days of any registered share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EGP 200,000 under the AML regime; suspension of voting and dividend rights until accurate UBO data is filed; potential criminal liability for knowingly submitting false statements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified audit is mandatory for all Egyptian LLCs except those expressly exempted under the Micro and Small Enterprises Law; automatic mandatory audit applies where annual turnover exceeds EGP 5,000,000, total assets exceed EGP 2,000,000, or the company holds any cross-border commercial litigation trust accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Financial Reporting Standards (EFRS), which are converged with IFRS; large taxpayers must also submit full IFRS-compliant statements to the Egyptian Tax Authority.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every transfer of shares, partnership interest, or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be evidenced by a notarized minutes or resolution and entered in the statutory register; the confirmed UBO schedule must be filed annually with GAFI by 31 March, and any ownership change during the year must be updated in the register and reported to GAFI within 30 days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – 1,200 per year for a qualified registered agent and licensed physical office address in Egypt
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – 8,000 depending on cross-border activity, multi-jurisdiction asset tracing volume, and number of IOLTA trust accounts

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 10-year income tax holiday for eligible investment zones and certain industries under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Free Zone entities exempt on export profits; 50% deduction for labour-intensive and logistics activities; accelerated depreciation on specialized equipment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Corporate Income Tax Declaration) filed electronically via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) portal at www.eta.gov.eg, integrated with the e-invoicing/e-receipt and tax-card validation systems.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance tax payments are separately required for taxpayers subject to Art. 86 of Law 91/2005.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months from the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is 30 April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Insert the Egyptian tax card number and commercial registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent or branch must use its optional Egyptian TIN; otherwise identify the Egyptian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate the start and end dates of the reporting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The period must match audited financials of the Egyptian branch or PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all gross receipts from litigation support, arbitration services, asset tracing fees, and reimbursable disbursements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include payments attributable to activities carried on in Egypt through a fixed place of business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State verifiable expenses deductible under Articles 30–39 of Law No. 91/2005, excluding non-deductible fines, reserves, and related-party charges above arm's-length values.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate common head-office expenses only if the PE benefit test and transfer pricing documentation are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determine book profit adjusted for statutory add-backs, transfer pricing adjustments, and prior-year loss offsets within the 5-year limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applicable only to the Egyptian PE's attributable profits; deferred service charges are disregarded unless substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 22.5% headline rate to taxable income, subtract quarterly advance payments, final WHT, and foreign tax credits; remit any remaining balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Proceed with the payment through the ETA e-collection service using the USD/EUR conversion instruction from the Central Bank of Egypt where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative fine of EGP 1,000–5,000 plus a 2% monthly late-payment surcharge on the outstanding tax (capped at 100%). False declarations or concealment of revenue additionally expose the taxpayer to criminal prosecution under Art. 133 Law 91/2005 and a fine of up to EGP 100,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain reduced DTA withholding, the non-resident shareholder must submit (i) a tax residency certificate (TRC) from the treaty country, (ii) audited proof of beneficial ownership, and (iii) a written waiver request to the ETA before distribution. The ETA will issue a reduced-rate clearance certificate after substance review; failure to pre-clear results in the full 20% statutory withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 20% for royalties and 20% for interest. Under Egypt's treaties, royalty rates are often reduced to 10–15% and interest to 10–15%, contingent on transparent ownership and anti-abuse clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not maintain standalone Economic Substance Regulations as in Gulf Cooperation Council states; however, the ETA applies the substance-over-form doctrine, beneficial ownership tests, and DTA anti-abuse rules. A foreign parent or treaty claimant must demonstrate actual commercial activity, local management, and substantive decision-making in its jurisdiction of residence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of Egyptian-source litigation revenues, fabrication of legal defense costs, or manual manipulation of accounting records to eliminate taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax, 2% monthly surcharge up to 100%, fine of up to EGP 100,000, and criminal prosecution for felony tax evasion under Art. 133 of Law No. 91/2005.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax; Egyptian courts routinely issue travel bans, freeze personal assets, and impose prison terms of 3–5 years upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare the Local File and Master File when controlled transactions exceed EGP 8 million, or charging non-arm's-length fees to foreign affiliate litigation chambers without current comparables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP adjustment at full corporate rate, solvency of a 30% penalty on the adjusted amount if documentation is incomplete, loss of deduction for the undocumented cross-border payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who sign false transfer pricing disclosures face personal civil liability for the tax differential, disqualification from board positions, and criminal referral for knowingly providing misleading documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Egyptian LLC exclusively as a conduit for routing cross-border litigation settlements to an inactive foreign principal without staff, office, or board activity in Egypt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, retroactive imposition of 20% dividend WHT on all distributions, deemed profit taxation, and revocation of the tax-registration certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced; directors are personally assessed for withheld taxes plus statutory penalties and may be banned from forming future entities in Egypt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving cross-border settlement or asset-tracing proceeds via uncqualified cryptocurrency, offshore shell accounts, or without reporting threshold transactions to the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit in violation of AML Law No. 80/2002.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EGP 1 million, freezing of IOLTA/trust accounts, confiscation of proceeds, and imprisonment of 5–10 years if linked to tax-evasion predicates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners are criminally liable; personal travel bans, seizure of personal property, and prohibition from financial services are commonly imposed.
